claims.paper_text: A lost submission response can leave a generation client uncertain whether its backend executed a request. We describe an evidence exporter, a same-run submission guard, and controlled fault injection for local image-generation pipelines. The exporter separates reported state, interpretation, and oracle evidence. Four fixed Windows/ComfyUI cases retained one execution binding per control and two per response-loss case; their second calls created fresh runs outside the guard. A subsequent same-run campaign initially stopped at model-identity validation. Restoring the pinned process-local inventory in a revised research caller exposed the guard: the retry returned submission-outcome-unknown with no additional submission, while the original run remained unresolved. Synthetic CPU fixtures expose incomplete operation as a cost. Raw payloads support reconstruction of the new retained bindings; the historical event gap remains. Original-run reconciliation, deployment rates, physical GPU execution counts and output-quality improvements remain unestablished.
